text:
**Findings**

High: [evalmerge/parsers.py](/work/evalmerge/parsers.py:203) lines 203-205 accepts non-dict `metrics` from Format B and then calls `.get`, crashing ingest instead of emitting a structured warning.

High: [evalmerge/parsers.py](/work/evalmerge/parsers.py:254) line 254 lets malformed XML raise `ParseError`, so one bad Format C file aborts the whole ingest.

High: [evalmerge/normalize.py](/work/evalmerge/normalize.py:83) lines 83-95 allow `nan`/non-finite scores through parsing and clamping; inserting `nan` hits SQLite `NOT NULL` as an `IntegrityError`.

Medium: [evalmerge/parsers.py](/work/evalmerge/parsers.py:202) lines 202-245 allow empty/missing `id`, `model_name`, and `benchmark` in Format B, producing canonical rows with empty identifiers/model/task and no warnings.

Medium: [evalmerge/parsers.py](/work/evalmerge/parsers.py:256) lines 256-324 allow missing XML `id`, `model`, and `task`, also producing empty canonical rows without warnings.

Medium: [evalmerge/parsers.py](/work/evalmerge/parsers.py:87) lines 87-91 and [evalmerge/parsers.py](/work/evalmerge/parsers.py:173) lines 173-174 read entire CSV/JSONL files into memory instead of streaming; large inputs can make ingest fail unnecessarily.

Low: [evalmerge/cli.py](/work/evalmerge/cli.py:44) lines 44-47 report “no input files” as an error only after `ingest()` has already created the SQLite database/schema.

**Score:** 6/10. The code is small, readable, and has a good fixture-driven test suite, but the validation contract is weaker than the README claims: malformed input can crash the pipeline or silently create bad canonical rows.

**Rewrite Estimate:** About 120 lines need significant change: parser validation/error handling, finite-number checks, streaming reads, CLI preflight behavior, and focused tests for those cases.

**Approval:** No, I would not approve this as-is for active development or production ingest.

Verification: `python -m pytest -q` passed 58 tests. `compileall` also passed when using `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp/pycache`; the default pycache location is read-only in this environment.
